passages.text: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Jonathan spoke to the young man who carried his armor.
Jonathan said, “Come with me.”
Jonathan said, “Let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.”
Jonathan did not tell his father.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹנָתָ֤ן בֶּן־ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ הַנַּ֙עַר֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו לְכָ֗ה וְנַעְבְּרָה֙ אֶל־ מַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַלָּ֑ז וּלְאָבִ֖יו לֹ֥א הִגִּֽיד׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men, including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul was sitting at the edge of Gibeah.
He was under a pomegranate tree in Migron.
About six hundred men were with Saul.
Ahijah was among them.
Ahijah wore an ephod.
Ahijah was the son of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the brother of Ichabod.
Ahitub was the son of Phinehas.
Phinehas was the son of Eli.
Eli was the priest of the LORD in Shiloh.
The people with Saul did not know that Jonathan had left.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֗וּל יוֹשֵׁב֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַגִּבְעָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת הָרִמּ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן וְהָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ כְּשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃ וַאֲחִיָּ֣ה בֶן־ אֲחִט֡וּב אֲחִ֡י אִיכָב֣וֹד׀ בֶּן־ פִּינְחָ֨ס בֶּן־ עֵלִ֜י כֹּהֵ֧ן׀ יְהוָ֛ה בְּשִׁל֖וֹ נֹשֵׂ֣א אֵפ֑וֹד וְהָעָם֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י הָלַ֖ךְ יוֹנָתָֽן׃

passages.text: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Jonathan wanted to cross a pass to reach the Philistine outpost.
There were cliffs on both sides of this pass.
One cliff stood on one side.
The other cliff stood on the other side.
The name of one cliff was Bozez.
The name of the other cliff was Seneh.
passages.original: וּבֵ֣ין הַֽמַּעְבְּר֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּקֵּ֤שׁ יֽוֹנָתָן֙ לַֽעֲבֹר֙ עַל־ מַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שֵׁן־ הַסֶּ֤לַע מֵהָעֵ֙בֶר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְשֵׁן־ הַסֶּ֥לַע מֵהָעֵ֖בֶר מִזֶּ֑ה וְשֵׁ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ בּוֹצֵ֔ץ וְשֵׁ֥ם הָאֶחָ֖ד סֶֽנֶּה׃

passages.text: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.
passages.sermon:
There were two cliffs.
One cliff stood on the north side.
This cliff faced Michmash.
The other cliff stood on the south side.
This cliff faced Geba.
passages.original: הַשֵּׁ֧ן הָאֶחָ֛ד מָצ֥וּק מִצָּפ֖וֹן מ֣וּל מִכְמָ֑שׂ וְהָאֶחָ֥ד מִנֶּ֖גֶב מ֥וּל גָּֽבַע׃ס

passages.text: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to the young man who carried his armor.
Jonathan said, “Come with me.
Let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men.
Perhaps the LORD will act for us.
Nothing can stop the LORD from saving.
The LORD can save by many people or by few people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל־ הַנַּ֣עַר׀ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו לְכָה֙ וְנַעְבְּרָ֗ה אֶל־ מַצַּב֙ הָעֲרֵלִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אוּלַ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לָ֑נוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לַֽיהוָה֙ מַעְצ֔וֹר לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ בְּרַ֖ב א֥וֹ בִמְעָֽט׃

passages.text: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan had an armor-bearer.
The armor-bearer spoke to Jonathan.
He said, “Do everything that is in your heart.”
He said, “Go ahead.”
He said, “I am with you.”
He said, “I am with you with all my heart.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו עֲשֵׂ֖ה כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ נְטֵ֣ה לָ֔ךְ הִנְנִ֥י עִמְּךָ֖ כִּלְבָבֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan was brave and trusted God.
Jonathan spoke to his armor-bearer.
Jonathan said, “We will cross over to these men.
We will show ourselves to them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֹבְרִ֖ים אֶל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִגְלִ֖ינוּ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to his armor-bearer.
Jonathan explained what to do.
Jonathan said, “If the Philistines say to us, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ we will stay where we are.
We will not go up to them.”
passages.original: אִם־ כֹּ֤ה יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ דֹּ֕מּוּ עַד־ הַגִּיעֵ֖נוּ אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְעָמַ֣דְנוּ תַחְתֵּ֔ינוּ וְלֹ֥א נַעֲלֶ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was a brave leader of Israel.
He spoke to his armor-bearer.
He said, "If the Philistines say, 'Come up to us,' we will go up."
This will be a sign for us.
The LORD has given the Philistines into our hands.
passages.original: וְאִם־ כֹּ֨ה יֹאמְר֜וּ עֲל֤וּ עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ וְעָלִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־ נְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדֵ֑נוּ וְזֶה־ לָּ֖נוּ הָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan and his armor-bearer revealed themselves.
They stood before the Philistine outpost.
The Philistine soldiers saw them.
The Philistines said, “Look!”
They said, “The Hebrews are coming out of the holes.”
They said, “These are the places where the Hebrews were hiding.”
passages.original: וַיִּגָּל֣וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֶל־ מַצַּ֖ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הִנֵּ֤ה עִבְרִים֙ יֹֽצְאִ֔ים מִן־ הַחֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִתְחַבְּאוּ־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan had an armor-bearer with him.
They approached a Philistine outpost.
The Philistine soldiers saw Jonathan and his armor-bearer.
The Philistine soldiers called out to them.
They said, “Come up to us.”
They said, “We will show you something.”
Jonathan spoke to his armor-bearer.
Jonathan said, “Follow me.”
Jonathan said, “The LORD has given the Philistines into Israel’s hand.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲנוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמַּצָּבָ֜ה אֶת־ יוֹנָתָ֣ן׀ וְאֶת־ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ עֲל֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנוֹדִ֥יעָה אֶתְכֶ֖ם דָּבָ֑ר פ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל־ נֹשֵׂ֤א כֵלָיו֙ עֲלֵ֣ה אַחֲרַ֔י כִּֽי־ נְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan was brave.
Jonathan climbed up.
He used his hands and feet to climb.
His armor-bearer followed him.
The Philistines stood in front of Jonathan.
The Philistines fell before Jonathan.
Jonathan’s armor-bearer came behind him.
The armor-bearer killed the Philistines who were still alive.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַל יוֹנָתָ֗ן עַל־ יָדָיו֙ וְעַל־ רַגְלָ֔יו וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו אַחֲרָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּלוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יוֹנָתָ֔ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו מְמוֹתֵ֥ת אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men over half an acre of land.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was a brave Israelite.
He had an armor-bearer with him.
They attacked the Philistines together.
This was their first attack.
Jonathan and his armor-bearer killed about twenty men.
They did this in an area about half an acre in size.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֞י הַמַּכָּ֣ה הָרִאשֹׁנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יוֹנָתָ֛ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו כְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים אִ֑ישׁ כְּבַחֲצִ֥י מַעֲנָ֖ה צֶ֥מֶד שָׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then terror struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked and panic spread from God.
passages.sermon:
God sent panic upon the Philistines.
Terror struck the Philistines in their camp.
Terror struck the Philistines in the field.
All the Philistine people felt fear.
The Philistine outposts trembled.
The Philistine raiding parties trembled.
The earth shook.
God caused this great panic.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי֩ חֲרָדָ֨ה בַמַּחֲנֶ֤ה בַשָּׂדֶה֙ וּבְכָל־ הָעָ֔ם הַמַּצָּב֙ וְהַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית חָרְד֖וּ גַּם־ הֵ֑מָּה וַתִּרְגַּ֣ז הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתְּהִ֖י לְחֶרְדַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction, Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had watchmen stationed at Gibeah in Benjamin.
The watchmen looked out over the land.
They saw the enemy troops.
The enemy troops were melting away.
The enemy troops scattered in every direction.
Saul spoke to the people with him.
He said, “Call the roll.
See who has left us.”
They called the roll.
They checked who was missing.
They saw that Jonathan was not there.
They saw that Jonathan’s armor-bearer was not there.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֤וּ הַצֹּפִים֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל בְּגִבְעַ֖ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וְהִנֵּ֧ה הֶהָמ֛וֹן נָמ֖וֹג וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַהֲלֹֽם׃פ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל לָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ פִּקְדוּ־ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ מִ֖י הָלַ֣ךְ מֵעִמָּ֑נוּ וַֽיִּפְקְד֔וּ וְהִנֵּ֛ה אֵ֥ין יוֹנָתָ֖ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Ahijah was a priest with Saul.
The ark of God was with the Israelites that day.
Saul spoke to Ahijah.
Saul said, “Bring the ark of God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ לַֽאֲחִיָּ֔ה הַגִּ֖ישָׁה אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּֽי־ הָיָ֞ה אֲר֧וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
A priest was with Saul.
Saul spoke to the priest.
At the same time, there was noise in the Philistine camp.
The noise in the Philistine camp kept getting louder.
Saul noticed the commotion was increasing.
Saul told the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י עַ֣ד דִּבֶּ֤ר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֶהָמ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וָרָ֑ב פ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר שָׁא֛וּל אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֱסֹ֥ף יָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
He gathered all the people who were with him.
They went together to the place of battle.
They saw the Philistines.
The Philistines were in great confusion.
Each Philistine fought against his own neighbor with the sword.
There was a very great chaos among the Philistines.
passages.original: וַיִּזָּעֵ֣ק שָׁא֗וּל וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה הָיְתָ֜ה חֶ֤רֶב אִישׁ֙ בְּרֵעֵ֔הוּ מְהוּמָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps of the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
passages.sermon:
Some Hebrews had joined the Philistines earlier.
These Hebrews had gone up and stayed in the Philistine camp.
Now these Hebrews left the Philistines.
They joined the Israelites.
The Israelites were with Saul and Jonathan.
passages.original: וְהָעִבְרִ֗ים הָי֤וּ לַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ כְּאֶתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָל֥וּ עִמָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה סָבִ֑יב וְגַם־ הֵ֗מָּה לִֽהְיוֹת֙ עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־ שָׁא֖וּל וְיוֹנָתָֽן׃

passages.text: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined Saul and Jonathan in the battle.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim.
They heard that the Philistines were fleeing.
These Israelites came out of hiding.
They joined Saul and Jonathan in the battle.
They pursued the Philistines.
passages.original: וְכֹל֩ אִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַמִּֽתְחַבְּאִ֤ים בְּהַר־ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי־ נָ֖סוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַֽיַּדְבְּק֥וּ גַם־ הֵ֛מָּה אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.
passages.sermon: The LORD saved Israel that day.\r\nThe battle moved past Beth-aven.
passages.original: וַיּ֧וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַ֨מִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָבְרָ֖ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The men of Israel fought in a battle that day.
Saul spoke to all the people.
He made them take an oath.
Saul said, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening.”
He said, “No one may eat until I have taken vengeance on my enemies.”
All the people obeyed Saul.
None of the troops ate any food that day.
passages.original: וְאִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נִגַּ֖שׂ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּאֶל֩ שָׁא֨וּל אֶת־ הָעָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר אָר֣וּר הָ֠אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ יֹ֨אכַל לֶ֜חֶם עַד־ הָעֶ֗רֶב וְנִקַּמְתִּי֙ מֵאֹ֣יְבַ֔י וְלֹֽא טָעַ֥ם כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם לָֽחֶם׃ס

passages.text: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.
passages.sermon: The men of Israel were soldiers.\r\nAll the soldiers entered the forest.\r\nThey saw honey on the ground.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֣אוּ בַיָּ֑עַר וַיְהִ֥י דְבַ֖שׁ עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel entered the forest.
They saw honey flowing on the ground.
No one put his hand to his mouth.
The men feared the oath Saul had made them take.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָעָם֙ אֶל־ הַיַּ֔עַר וְהִנֵּ֖ה הֵ֣לֶךְ דְּבָ֑שׁ וְאֵין־ מַשִּׂ֤יג יָדוֹ֙ אֶל־ פִּ֔יו כִּֽי־ יָרֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם אֶת־ הַשְּׁבֻעָֽה׃

passages.text: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had charged the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had commanded the people not to eat that day.
Jonathan did not hear his father give this command.
Jonathan held a staff in his hand.
He reached out the end of his staff.
He dipped the end of his staff into the honeycomb.
He put his hand to his mouth.
His eyes became bright.
passages.original: וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן לֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֗ע בְּהַשְׁבִּ֣יעַ אָבִיו֮ אֶת־ הָעָם֒ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶת־ קְצֵ֤ה הַמַּטֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיִּטְבֹּ֥ל אוֹתָ֖הּ בְּיַעְרַ֣ת הַדְּבָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֤שֶׁב יָדוֹ֙ אֶל־ פִּ֔יו וַתָּרֹאנָה עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”
passages.sermon:
A man from among the people answered Jonathan.
He spoke to Jonathan.
He said, "Your father made the people take a solemn oath."
He said, "He commanded the people."
He said, 'Cursed is the man who eats food today.'"
The people are faint because of this oath.
passages.original: וַיַּעַן֩ אִ֨ישׁ מֵֽהָעָ֜ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַשְׁבֵּעַ֩ הִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ אָבִ֤יךָ אֶת־ הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָר֥וּר הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ יֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם הַיּ֑וֹם וַיָּ֖עַף הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to the people.
Jonathan said, “My father has brought trouble to the land.”
Jonathan told them to look at him.
Jonathan said, “See how my eyes have brightened.”
Jonathan explained why his eyes were bright.
Jonathan said, “My eyes are bright because I tasted a little of this honey.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יֽוֹנָתָ֔ן עָכַ֥ר אָבִ֖י אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ רְאוּ־ נָא֙ כִּֽי־ אֹ֣רוּ עֵינַ֔י כִּ֣י טָעַ֔מְתִּי מְעַ֖ט דְּבַ֥שׁ הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to the people.
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Jonathan said the people would have done better if they had eaten today.
The people had taken food from their enemies as plunder.
Jonathan said the people should have eaten from this plunder.
If the people had eaten, they would have been stronger.
Jonathan said the people would have defeated more Philistines if they had eaten.
The victory over the Philistines was not as great as it could have been.
passages.original: אַ֗ף כִּ֡י לוּא֩ אָכֹ֨ל אָכַ֤ל הַיּוֹם֙ הָעָ֔ם מִשְּׁלַ֥ל אֹיְבָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָצָ֑א כִּ֥י עַתָּ֛ה לֹֽא־ רָבְתָ֥ה מַכָּ֖ה בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites fought the Philistines that day.
They struck down the Philistines.
They fought from Michmash to Aijalon.
The people became very tired.
The people became very weak.
passages.original: וַיַּכּ֞וּ בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מִמִּכְמָ֖שׂ אַיָּלֹ֑נָה וַיָּ֥עַף הָעָ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel fought the Philistines that day.
They became very tired and hungry.
The people rushed to the plunder.
They took sheep, cattle, and calves from the enemy.
They slaughtered the animals on the ground.
The people ate the meat while the blood was still in it.
passages.original: וַיַּעַשׂ הָעָם֙ אֶל־ שָׁלָל וַיִּקְח֨וּ צֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר וּבְנֵ֥י בָקָ֖ר וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ־ אָ֑רְצָה וַיֹּ֥אכַל הָעָ֖ם עַל־ הַדָּֽם׃

passages.text: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.” “You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Someone came to Saul.
The person spoke to Saul.
The person said, “Look, the people are sinning against the LORD.
They are eating meat with the blood still in it.”
Saul answered them.
Saul said, “You have broken faith.”
Saul gave a command.
Saul said, “Roll a large stone over here at once.”
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לְשָׁאוּל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה הָעָ֛ם חֹטִ֥אים לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עַל־ הַדָּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בְּגַדְתֶּ֔ם גֹּֽלּוּ־ אֵלַ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֶ֥בֶן גְּדוֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’ ” So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his people.
He said, “Go among the people.
Tell them this message.
Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep.
You must slaughter the animal here.
Then you may eat the meat.
Do not sin against the LORD.
Do not eat meat with the blood still in it.”
That night, every man brought his ox.
Each man held his ox in his hand.
They slaughtered the animals there.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֣וּל פֻּ֣צוּ בָעָ֡ם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם לָהֶ֡ם הַגִּ֣ישׁוּ אֵלַי֩ אִ֨ישׁ שׁוֹר֜וֹ וְאִ֣ישׁ שְׂיֵ֗הוּ וּשְׁחַטְתֶּ֤ם בָּזֶה֙ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ תֶחֶטְא֥וּ לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶל־ הַדָּ֑ם וַיַּגִּ֨שׁוּ כָל־ הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ שׁוֹר֧וֹ בְיָד֛וֹ הַלַּ֖יְלָה וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul built an altar.
He built the altar for the LORD.
This was the first altar Saul built for the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁא֛וּל מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה אֹת֣וֹ הֵחֵ֔ל לִבְנ֥וֹת מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied. But the priest said, “We must consult God here.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his troops.
Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines tonight.
Let us attack them until morning.
Let us not leave any man alive among them.”
The troops answered Saul.
They said, “Do what seems good to you.”
A priest was present.
The priest spoke.
The priest said, “We must consult God here.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֡וּל נֵרְדָ֣ה אַחֲרֵי֩ פְלִשְׁתִּ֨ים׀ לַ֜יְלָה וְֽנָבֹ֥זָה בָהֶ֣ם׀ עַד־ א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר וְלֹֽא־ נַשְׁאֵ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כָּל־ הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵׂ֑הס וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נִקְרְבָ֥ה הֲלֹ֖ם אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: So Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?” But God did not answer him that day.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to God.
Saul asked God a question.
Saul said, “Should I go down after the Philistines?”
Saul also asked, “Will You give the Philistines into the hand of Israel?”
God did not answer Saul that day.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל שָׁאוּל֙ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים הַֽאֵרֵד֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הֲתִתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א עָנָ֖הוּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: Therefore Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops, and let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to the leaders of the troops.
Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the people.”
Saul wanted to find out about a sin that happened that day.
Saul said, “Let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל גֹּ֣שֽׁוּ הֲלֹ֔ם כֹּ֖ל פִּנּ֣וֹת הָעָ֑ם וּדְע֣וּ וּרְא֔וּ בַּמָּ֗ה הָֽיְתָ֛ה הַחַטָּ֥את הַזֹּ֖את הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: As surely as the LORD who saves Israel lives, even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!” But not one of the troops said a word.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The LORD saves Israel.
The LORD lives.
Saul spoke to the people.
Saul said, “As surely as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if the sinner is Jonathan my son, he must die.”
None of the people answered Saul.
No one from the troops said anything.
passages.original: כִּ֣י חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה הַמּוֹשִׁ֙יעַ֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֧י אִם־ יֶשְׁנ֛וֹ בְּיוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנִ֖י כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת יָמ֑וּת וְאֵ֥ין עֹנֵ֖הוּ מִכָּל־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Saul said to all Israel, “You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to all the people of Israel.
He said, “You stand on one side.”
He said, “I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.”
The people answered Saul.
They said, “Do what seems good to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַתֶּם֙ תִּֽהְיוּ֙ לְעֵ֣בֶר אֶחָ֔ד וַֽאֲנִי֙ וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנִ֔י נִהְיֶ֖ה לְעֵ֣בֶר אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה׃ס

passages.text: So Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Why have You not answered Your servant this day? If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim; but if the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected, but the people were cleared of the charge.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Saul asked God for an answer.
Saul said, “Why have You not answered Your servant today?”
Saul wanted to know who was at fault.
Saul said, “If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim.”
Saul said, “If the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.”
God gave an answer.
Jonathan and Saul were chosen.
The people of Israel were not chosen.
The people were cleared of the charge.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל אֶל־ יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָ֣בָה תָמִ֑ים וַיִּלָּכֵ֧ד יוֹנָתָ֛ן וְשָׁא֖וּל וְהָעָ֥ם יָצָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Saul spoke to the people.
Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.”
They cast the lot.
The lot selected Jonathan.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הַפִּ֕ילוּ בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֖ין יוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנִ֑י וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד יוֹנָתָֽן׃

passages.text: “Tell me what you have done,” Saul commanded him. So Jonathan told him, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Saul spoke to Jonathan.
Saul said, “Tell me what you have done.”
Jonathan answered Saul.
Jonathan said, “I tasted a little honey.”
Jonathan used the end of the staff in his hand to taste the honey.
Jonathan said, “Now I must die?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ י֣וֹנָתָ֔ן הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָה וַיַּגֶּד־ ל֣וֹ יוֹנָתָ֗ן וַיֹּאמֶר֩ טָעֹ֨ם טָעַ֜מְתִּי בִּקְצֵ֨ה הַמַּטֶּ֧ה אֲשֶׁר־ בְּיָדִ֛י מְעַ֥ט דְּבַ֖שׁ הִנְנִ֥י אָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: And Saul declared, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Jonathan, his son.
Saul made a solemn declaration.
Saul said, “May God punish me if I do not do this.”
Saul said, “May God punish me even more if I fail.”
Saul said, “Jonathan, you must surely die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֑ף כִּֽי־ מ֥וֹת תָּמ֖וּת יוֹנָתָֽן׃

passages.text: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die—he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God’s help he has accomplished this today.” So the people rescued Jonathan, and he did not die.
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Saul.
They said, “Should Jonathan die?
Jonathan brought a great deliverance to Israel.
Never!
As surely as the LORD lives, not a single hair of his head will fall to the ground.
God helped Jonathan today.
Jonathan accomplished this with God.
The people rescued Jonathan.
Jonathan did not die.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם אֶל־ שָׁא֗וּל הֲֽיוֹנָתָ֤ן׀ יָמוּת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָ֠שָׂה הַיְשׁוּעָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל֒ חָלִ֗ילָה חַי־ יְהוָה֙ אִם־ יִפֹּ֞ל מִשַּׂעֲרַ֤ת רֹאשׁוֹ֙ אַ֔רְצָה כִּֽי־ עִם־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּפְדּ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אֶת־ יוֹנָתָ֖ן וְלֹא־ מֵֽת׃ס

passages.text: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.
passages.sermon: Saul was the king of Israel.\r\nSaul stopped chasing the Philistines.\r\nThe Philistines went back to their own land.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַל שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָלְכ֥וּ לִמְקוֹמָֽם׃

passages.text: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side—the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he routed them.
passages.sermon:
Saul became king over Israel.
He fought against all his enemies around him.
He fought the Moabites.
He fought the Ammonites.
He fought the Edomites.
He fought the kings of Zobah.
He fought the Philistines.
Wherever Saul turned, he defeated his enemies.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֛וּל לָכַ֥ד הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם סָבִ֣יב׀ בְּֽכָל־ אֹיְבָ֡יו בְּמוֹאָ֣ב׀ וּבִבְנֵי־ עַמּ֨וֹן וּבֶאֱד֜וֹם וּבְמַלְכֵ֤י צוֹבָה֙ וּבַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּבְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִפְנֶ֖ה יַרְשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul fought bravely.
Saul attacked the Amalekites.
Saul defeated the Amalekites.
Saul saved Israel.
He rescued Israel from those who plundered them.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חַ֔יִל וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד שֹׁסֵֽהוּ׃ס

passages.text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had three sons.
Their names were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua.
Saul had two daughters.
The older daughter was named Merab.
The younger daughter was named Michal.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל יוֹנָתָ֥ן וְיִשְׁוִ֖י וּמַלְכִּי־ שׁ֑וּעַ וְשֵׁם֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו שֵׁ֤ם הַבְּכִירָה֙ מֵרַ֔ב וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה מִיכַֽל׃

passages.text: His wife’s name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Saul’s uncle Ner.
passages.sermon:
Saul had a wife named Ahinoam.
Ahinoam was the daughter of Ahimaaz.
Saul had a commander for his army.
The commander’s name was Abner.
Abner was the son of Ner.
Ner was Saul’s uncle.
passages.original: וְשֵׁם֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת שָׁא֔וּל אֲחִינֹ֖עַם בַּת־ אֲחִימָ֑עַץ וְשֵׁ֤ם שַׂר־ צְבָאוֹ֙ אֲבִינֵ֔ר בֶּן־ נֵ֖ר דּ֥וֹד שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: Saul’s father Kish and Abner’s father Ner were sons of Abiel.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the son of Kish.
Abner was the son of Ner.
Kish and Ner were both sons of Abiel.
Abiel was the grandfather of Saul and Abner.
passages.original: וְקִ֧ישׁ אֲבִֽי־ שָׁא֛וּל וְנֵ֥ר אֲבִֽי־ אַבְנֵ֖ר בֶּן־ אֲבִיאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
There was war between Israel and the Philistines.
The war was fierce.
The war lasted all the days of Saul’s reign.
Saul looked for strong men.
Saul looked for brave men.
Whenever Saul saw a strong or brave man, he took him.
Saul gathered these men to himself.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ חֲזָקָ֣ה עַל־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְרָאָ֨ה שָׁא֜וּל כָּל־ אִ֤ישׁ גִּבּוֹר֙ וְכָל־ בֶּן־ חַ֔יִל וַיַּאַסְפֵ֖הוּ אֵלָֽיו׃ס
